articles.title: Architect Andrew Batey designed this 1972 glass house for a photographer; the Berkeley Hills home with a former darkroom is listed for $1.088 million
articles.summary: A glass house nestled among the trees of California’s Berkeley Hills is attracting attention for its unusual architecture and creative history.
articles.body: A glass house nestled among the trees of California’s Berkeley Hills is attracting attention for its unusual architecture and creative history. Designed in 1972 by architect Andrew Batey for architectural photographer Henry Bowles, the residence was conceived to connect its interiors with the surrounding woodland. The two-bedroom property combines glass, steel and redwood in a design that makes natural light and the landscape central to its character. Now listed for $1.088 million, the home is being offered after more than two decades under its current owner. Its former photographic darkroom, double-height living room and distinctive glass façade add to its appeal.Andrew Batey designed the Berkeley glass house for photographer Henry BowlesThe story of the Photographer’s House began in 1972, when architectural photographer Henry Bowles commissioned a residence that reflected his appreciation for design and natural light. According to SFGATE, Bowles had trained under renowned Western photographer Morley Baer before establishing his own professional reputation. Architect Andrew Batey, who was 28 when he undertook the project, designed the house using glass, steel and redwood. The commission brought together Bowles’s interest in architectural photography and Batey’s developing modernist approach. The residence is identified as one of Batey’s early commissions, predating his subsequent work with architect Mark Mack at the firm Batey and Mack. The house therefore offers a glimpse into the architect’s early career while preserving the creative vision behind its original commission.The two-storey glass façade brings Berkeley’s woodland into the homeThe property’s defining feature is its expansive glass façade, which creates a visual connection between the interior and the wooded hillside outside. According to the New York Post, the 1,625-square-foot house combines glass, steel and redwood to create a distinctive modernist residence. Its double-height living room gives the relatively compact home a sense of openness, while sliding glass doors lead towards a spacious deck. Realtor also highlighted the two-storey glass wall as a defining feature of the property, helping explain its appeal to readers interested in distinctive homes. Rather than placing conventional walls between residents and the landscape, the design allows trees and daylight to become part of the visual experience. The combination of exposed structural elements and extensive glazing gives the house a character that remains closely tied to its woodland setting.A floating staircase, loft bedroom and skylit bathroom shape the interiorInside, the Photographer’s House combines an open layout with architectural details that distinguish it from a conventional two-bedroom residence. SFGATE describes a double-height living area with exposed beams, alongside an updated kitchen featuring quartz countertops and custom honeycomb tile. A floating staircase with cable railing connects the main living space to the upper level, where a 400-square-foot mezzanine accommodates the second bedroom among the oak treetops. The primary suite has its own entrance, adding a degree of separation within the home’s open design. Another notable feature is the black-tiled bathroom, illuminated by two skylights. Batey returned in the late 1980s to design the bathroom, extending his involvement with the property beyond its original construction. These details combine contemporary updates with the architectural character of the original house.The former darkroom adds a creative legacy to the $1.088 million listingThe property’s history as a photographer’s residence extends beyond its main living spaces. Batey originally built a darkroom beside the single-car garage, providing Bowles with a dedicated space for photographic work. The approximately 300-square-foot area now features a skylight and offers potential for use as a studio, guest space or home office. The current owner, Mike Moye, discovered the property in 2003 after a photograph of its glass façade caught his attention. He subsequently spent more than two decades living in and updating the residence, including improvements to the kitchen and outdoor areas. Realtor reported that the property became the most popular home on its weekly list, demonstrating the online interest generated by its unusual design. Listed for $1.088 million, the Berkeley Hills house brings together architectural history, woodland views and adaptable creative space.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.body: Fortnite star Cody “Clix” has called out Victor “VicterV”’s father, known online as Papa Vic or Pops, accusing him of hurting his son’s reputation through repeated comments about other players. Their disagreement began in May 2026, when Pops claimed VicterV could beat Clix despite their differences in competitive results. The dispute grew after Clix won a Divisional Cup and later faced VicterV during the Solo FNCS event. Clix now says the father’s public comments are putting unnecessary pressure on the young player, who is trying to build his own career.May 2026: Cody Clix and Papa Vic trade shots over VicterV’s Fortnite resultsThe argument began when XSET player Faxuty spoke to Pops on Discord about his son’s ability to compete against Clix. Faxuty said, “Respectfully, I don’t even think [VicterV] could beat Clix.”Pops disagreed, replying, “Vic could beat Clix on 40 ping… We could beat Clix on high ping.”The conversation also turned to tournament results. Pops questioned Clix’s Tier 1 status, saying, “Victor got 33rd at LAN, by the way… tier one my ***.” He later called Clix and his teammate Higgs a “trash duo.”Clix responded after winning a Fortnite Divisional Cup in May. He directly challenged Pops, saying, “What the **** you got to say now, Pops? Your ******* IGL… dead last. Dead ******* last.”He also questioned VicterV’s performance in the West region, saying, “How does your son not get top 50 on West to qualify? My grandmother could ******* do that, and she’s ******* 90.”Pops dismissed the tournament result, replying, “Nobody gives a f about no Div Cup, bro.”The exchange set the stage for another confrontation months later, when their disagreement moved from tournament results to accusations about public attention and a player’s reputation.October 2026: Cody Clix accuses Papa Vic of clipfarming and pressuring VicterVThe dispute flared up again during the Solo FNCS event after VicterV contested Clix’s Point of Interest (POI), the location where a player chooses to land on the map. Clix eliminated VicterV during the match and said, “That’s what happens when your dad ****-talks for you. *******, GGs buddy.”During a call hosted by Faxuty, Clix criticised Pops for speaking publicly on his son’s behalf. He said, “I’ve never seen a 50-year-old dad speak on behalf of their son on a professional video game… it comes off like you’re trying to use your son to capitalize on clout, exposure, views, and impressions.”Pops later accused Clix of taking the disagreement too far. In a phone call with Faxuty, he said, “Clix is trying to make it personal when you don’t gotta make it personal. He gon’ get what he wants. If he asks for it, he shall receive.”Clix addressed the issue again on his alternate X account, @clixprivalt. He argued that Pops’ actions were doing more harm than good and putting pressure on VicterV, whom he described as a sweet kid trying to compete.Clix wrote, “I’ve seen a lot of the parents of players support their kids but the level that Victor V’s dad is doing it is actually doing a lot more harm than good, calling me out saying a bunch of nonsense months ago then playing victim card saying I’m trying to make things personal is very interesting alongside putting this amount of pressure on your child when Victor is just a sweet kid trying to compete is not the way to do it. Not trying to tell a father how to be a father but disappointed to see a player’s dad clipfarming & ruining the kid’s reputation instead of just supporting his son.”The comments show that Clix’s main concern is no longer just their competitive rivalry. He believes Pops’ public involvement is affecting how people see VicterV, while Pops has pushed back against Clix’s response.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.summary: US Senator Bernie Sanders has criticised Elon Musk for spending $366 million to support Republicans in the upcoming midterm elections, pointing to the
articles.body: US Senator Bernie Sanders has criticised Elon Musk for spending $366 million to support Republicans in the upcoming midterm elections, pointing to the tech billionaire’s sharp rise in wealth since backing President Donald Trump’s election campaign.Sanders said Musk had spent $290 million to help elect Trump and had since become $696 billion richer, becoming the world’s first trillionaire. He added that Musk was now spending $366 million to help Republicans retain control of Congress."Elon Musk spent $290 million to elect Trump. It paid off. Since his election, Musk got $696 billion richer & became the world’s 1st trillionaire. But that’s not enough. Now, Musk is spending $366 million to keep Republicans in control of Congress. STOP MUSK. STOP OLIGARCHY," Sanders said in a post on X.This comes as Elon Musk said that Starlink’s entry into India would benefit consumers by offering them more choices, arguing that Reliance Industries chairman Mukesh Ambani would remain in business even if competition reduced his profits.In a post on X, Musk criticised what he described as arguments by Ambani’s supporters against Starlink’s entry into the Indian market, calling them “absurd hypocrisy and hyperbole”.“On the one hand, they say Starlink couldn’t possibly compete with the amazing low prices offered by Ambani’s de facto monopoly in India and then, in the same breath, they essentially claim that Starlink would be too strong of a competitor!” Musk wrote.“The reality is that competition would greatly benefit the average citizen in India by giving them more choices, as it always does. Ambani’s profits will be lower, but he is not going out of business,” he added.Musk’s remarks follow an earlier post on Friday in which he addressed Ambani as “Prime Minister Ambani” and accused him of being the “real boss of India”.“Dear Prime Minister Ambani, Please accept my humble apologies for not realizing that you are the real boss of India. Naturally, you would prefer to maintain your monopolistic exploitation of the great people of India, but would you nonetheless consider allowing Starlink to compete?” Musk wrote.The billionaire has also alleged that unnamed business groups are trying to block Starlink’s entry into India to protect their market positions. The government has rejected these allegations, maintaining that the delay is due to pending regulatory and security requirements.Musk’s $276 million push to back RepublicansAccording to a report by The New York Times on Monday, Musk has spent $276 million since July alone, including $158 million through a super PAC focused on Republican Senate candidates. The report identified him as the largest single donor this year.Musk, considered a close ally of Trump, served as a special government adviser to the White House last year. His political action committee, America PAC, has confirmed the spending figures.Andrew Romeo, a spokesperson for America PAC, defended the expenditure, saying it was necessary to prevent Democrats from taking control of Congress in the midterm elections.“These robust investments have allowed the GOP apparatus to get its message out so Republicans can have a fighting chance to defy history,” Romeo told The New York Times.The spending comes as Republican candidates contend with Trump’s low approval ratings and growing concerns among voters over the cost of living. Democrats are seeking to capitalise on dissatisfaction with the president’s tenure and regain control of Congress, where Republicans currently hold majorities in both the House of Representatives and the Senate.You use AI every day. articles.title: Netanyahu seeks Saudi nod for Israel to join strikes on Houthis: Report
articles.summary: Israeli prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu is seeking Saudi Arabia’s approval for Israel to join the military campaign against Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthi
articles.body: Israeli prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu is seeking Saudi Arabia’s approval for Israel to join the military campaign against Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthi rebels, with the US mediating between the two sides, Israeli publication Haaretz reported, citing a diplomatic source.However, Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman is opposed to Israeli military involvement, fearing it could trigger a backlash among the kingdom’s public, the source said.Another source familiar with the matter said Netanyahu’s push was also aimed at strengthening ties with Riyadh and laying the groundwork for a future normalisation agreement between the two countries.US president Donald Trump has repeatedly advocated normalising Saudi-Israeli relations under the Abraham Accords. A potential agreement appeared close in 2023, before Hamas’s October 7 attack and the subsequent war in Gaza derailed regional diplomatic efforts.Saudi Arabia has maintained that it will not normalise ties with Israel without substantial progress towards establishing a Palestinian state. Netanyahu, meanwhile, has opposed Palestinian statehood, leaving a major obstacle to any agreement.Houthis intensify attacks on Saudi ArabiaThe diplomatic push comes as Saudi Arabia faces a series of Houthi attacks, including strikes on Riyadh’s King Khalid International Airport. A ballistic missile strike on Saturday killed at least 12 people and injured 309, while an attack on Sunday killed one person and wounded 1.Netanyahu condemned Saturday’s airport attack, calling it a “horrific terrorist attack” and expressing condolences to the victims’ families on behalf of Israel.The Houthis have targeted Saudi airports and oil installations in recent days amid an intensifying conflict in Yemen. The developments have raised concerns over regional security and the safety of key shipping routes, including the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, through which a significant share of global trade passes.Any Israeli intervention would risk complicating Saudi Arabia’s position in the conflict, particularly given domestic opposition to closer ties with Israel amid the unresolved Palestinian issue. Riyadh’s approval remains a key hurdle to Netanyahu’s reported effort to bring Israel into the campaign.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: A pilot project backed by Elton John’s foundation helped expand ‘opt-out HIV’ testing from two London hospitals to 89 emergency departments across England
articles.summary: A pilot project supported by the Elton John AIDS Foundation has helped transform how HIV testing is offered in England, expanding a programme first
articles.body: A pilot project supported by the Elton John AIDS Foundation has helped transform how HIV testing is offered in England, expanding a programme first introduced in two South London hospitals to 89 emergency departments across the country. The initiative makes HIV tests a routine part of emergency care, allowing patients to be tested unless they choose to decline. The approach aims to identify people who may be living with HIV without knowing it and connect them with treatment. Its expansion follows evidence that routine testing can reach people who might otherwise miss opportunities for diagnosis and care.How did the Elton John-backed pilot expand HIV testing across EnglandThe Elton John AIDS Foundation began pioneering opt-out HIV testing in South London in 2018. The initial work demonstrated how emergency departments could help identify people living with HIV who had not previously been diagnosed or who had become disconnected from treatment.According to the Foundation’s annual report, the pilot began in two South London hospitals and helped establish a model that could be extended across the NHS. The programme has since been scaled up, with government funding supporting its expansion to 89 emergency departments across England.The Foundation’s report on pilot schemes to accelerate access to pre-exposure prophylaxis, commonly known as PrEP, also highlights the wider importance of identifying HIV infections early. The initiative has reportedly led to 1,000 new HIV diagnoses through the expanded testing programme, demonstrating the potential of emergency departments to reach people who may not otherwise seek an HIV test.Why does opt-out testing make a differenceUnder an opt-out approach, HIV testing is offered routinely as part of a patient's hospital care rather than relying entirely on individuals to request it. Patients can decline the test, but the default offer helps make testing a normal part of healthcare.This matters because some people may not recognise their potential exposure to HIV or may feel uncomfortable asking for a test. Others may avoid testing because of stigma or assumptions about who is likely to acquire the virus.The Elton John AIDS Foundation explains that routine testing can help address these barriers by making the offer more inclusive. Its work has also shown the value of reaching people from communities that have historically faced inequalities in HIV testing and access to treatment.The Foundation’s HIV Social Impact Bond programme found that emergency departments and primary care settings were particularly effective in identifying Black African, Black Caribbean and Black Other women and girls living with HIV who might not have been tested elsewhere.What did the original South London programme achieveThe original initiative developed through a partnership involving the Elton John AIDS Foundation, Lambeth, Southwark and Lewisham councils, the National Lottery Community Fund, ViiV Healthcare, Comic Relief and Big Issue.The Foundation’s account of its UK Social Impact Bond describes the programme as the world's first social impact bond focused on bringing people living with HIV into care. It ran for 3 years, from 2018-21, across the 3 South London boroughs.The programme combined HIV testing in hospital emergency departments, HIV clinics, GP surgeries and community settings. Providers received payments based on results, including identifying people newly diagnosed with HIV and helping those who had stopped treatment return to care.Over the three-year period, more than 265,000 people received HIV tests. More than 460 people living with HIV entered treatment, including people who received a new diagnosis and those who returned to care after previously stopping treatment.The Foundation estimated that the programme helped avoid £90 million in healthcare costs. Earlier diagnosis and timely treatment can reduce the likelihood of people becoming seriously ill, while helping prevent further HIV transmission.How has the programme influenced national HIV policyThe results of the South London project helped build the case for extending routine HIV testing beyond the original locations. According to the Foundation’s UK Social Impact Bond, evidence from the initiative informed the work of the HIV Commission, parliamentary inquiries into HIV testing and the impact of HIV on ethnic minority communities, and the development of the government’s HIV Action Plan.In December 2021, the government announced £20 million in funding for emergency department HIV testing in areas with particularly high rates of new infections. This marked an important step towards making the approach available to more patients across England.The Foundation’s announcement on new funding to end HIV cases in England describes opt-out testing as a way to address inequalities in diagnosis and bring people into care earlier. The wider rollout also reflects the argument that HIV testing should not depend solely on whether someone visits a specialist sexual health service.Why is prevention also central to the effortFinding people who are already living with HIV is only one part of the effort to reduce new infections. Prevention measures, including access to PrEP, are also important.PrEP is medication taken by HIV-negative people to reduce their risk of acquiring the virus. The Elton John AIDS Foundation states that it can reduce the risk of acquiring HIV through sex by around 99% when taken as prescribed. In England, it has been available free through NHS sexual health clinics since the end of the PrEP Impact Trial in 2020.The Foundation’s pilot schemes initiative highlights the need to improve access to prevention alongside testing and treatment. Its approach recognises that people need to know their HIV status, understand their prevention options and be able to obtain appropriate support without unnecessary barriers.The Foundation has also called for public health investment that can demonstrate long-term benefits. Preventing new infections and connecting people to treatment can reduce future pressure on health services, while helping individuals receive care before their condition worsens.The 2030 goal depends on sustained investmentThe expansion to 89 emergency departments represents a significant development in England’s effort to identify undiagnosed HIV and improve access to treatment. However, the Foundation’s work also points to the need for continued investment in prevention, testing and support for people living with the virus.Its 2025 annual report records the programme’s development from a pilot in two South London hospitals into a model being scaled nationally. The report also links the wider rollout to the government’s £170 million HIV Action Plan, announced on World AIDS Day, and its commitment to ending new HIV transmissions by 2030.The Foundation has argued that proven approaches need sustained government backing if they are to reach more people.You use AI every day. articles.body: NEW DELHI: Delhi Police has registered multiple FIRs at Barakhamba Road and Tilak Marg police stations in connection with the Opposition’s protest on Monday. The cases relate to alleged barricade-breaking and graffiti on roads during the demonstration, police said.On Monday, INDIA bloc leaders and supporters, led by Rahul Gandhi, marched along Barakhamba Road towards the Supreme Court. Later, 11 opposition leaders filed a petition in the apex court challenging the Election Commission’s decisions regarding the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.In a parallel development, the Supreme Court Registry has flagged 14 defects in a writ petition filed by Rahul Gandhi, Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge and nine other INDIA bloc leaders challenging aspects of the Election Commission of India’s (ECI) ongoing Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.The petitioners include Trinamool Congress MP Saugata Roy, Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav, Rashtriya Janata Dal leader Tejashwi Yadav, Shiv Sena (UBT) MP Sanjay Raut, CPI(M) MP MA Baby, CPI leader D Raja, Jharkhand Mukti Morcha MP Mahua Majhi, NCP (SCP) MP Supriya Sule and Indian Union Muslim League MP ET Mohammed Basheer.The Registry has also sought clarification on why Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and Election Commissioners SS Sandhu and Vivek Joshi have been named as respondents in the petition, which has been filed under Article 32 of the Constitution.The petitioners have approached the Supreme Court alleging irregularities in the exercise of the Election Commission’s powers during the SIR. They have sought, among other reliefs, scrutiny of the manner in which the poll panel took and implemented decisions related to the revision of electoral rolls.Meanwhile, Delhi Police has sought an extension of the deployment of 273 companies of the Central Armed Police Forces (CAPF) in the national capital till October 20, citing the possibility of protests by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) and other organisations, PTI reported, quoting sources.The deployment was scheduled to end on Monday. Police has approached the Union home ministry, citing the need to maintain law and order and manage potential demonstrations at sensitive locations, including Jantar Mantar, the Election Commission, Parliament House and India Gate.Police have also flagged possible protests by the Bhim Army, student groups and other political organisations.A total of 301 CAPF companies were approved for deployment in Delhi, with 221 arriving on October 6 and another 80 approved on October 8. Of the additional 80 companies, 28 had not reported to Delhi Police as of Monday, the sources said.Rahul has also invited opposition MPs for high tea at his residence on Tuesday.This comes amid protests against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.Over the weekend, security was tightened across Delhi, 45 metro stations were closed and checks intensified at the city’s borders.Thousands of protesters, including CJP leaders and former chief ministers, were detained.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Bought Rs 25.21 lakh Maruti Invicto, found repainted parts; consumer court orders Rs 3.6 lakh relief
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: A district consumer commission in Kerala has directed an authorised Maruti Suzuki dealer to replace a Rs 25.21 lakh Invicto car after a buyer
articles.body: NEW DELHI: A district consumer commission in Kerala has directed an authorised Maruti Suzuki dealer to replace a Rs 25.21 lakh Invicto car after a buyer alleged that its bonnet, left door and upper portion had been repainted before delivery without his knowledge. Alternatively, the dealer must pay Rs 2 lakh towards repairs, Rs 1.5 lakh as compensation for mental agony and Rs 10,000 in litigation costs.The District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission, Kannur, passed the order on September 25, 2026, in a complaint filed against an authorised Maruti dealer.Why did the Maruti Invicto buyer complain?According to the commission order, Vijesh booked a blue Maruti Suzuki Invicto Strong Hybrid Zeta+ 7-seater on October 19, 2024, and received the vehicle on November 19, 2024. The sale price was Rs 25,21,000.He told the commission that he had inspected the car at the dealer's godown before delivery and was satisfied with its model, colour and condition. However, after taking delivery, he noticed that the upper portion, bonnet and left door appeared to have been freshly painted.Vijesh alleged that the repainting had been carried out without his consent or knowledge and had affected the car's original paint quality. He suspected the work might have been done to conceal damage caused by an accident or another incident before delivery.He asked the dealer to take back the vehicle and refund the amount paid. After the dealer allegedly refused, he sent a legal notice in January 2025, seeking relief. According to the order, the dealer neither complied with the demand nor replied to the notice.The buyer subsequently approached the consumer commission, seeking replacement of the car, Rs 10 lakh in compensation for mental agony and the costs of the proceedings.What did the expert report reveal about the car?The dealer did not appear before the commission or file a written response despite receiving notice. The case therefore proceeded ex parte, meaning it was heard in the dealer's absence.The bench of President Ravi Susha and members Molykutty Mathew and Sajeesh K.P commission said the buyer still had to establish his allegations.An expert commissioner, appointed on the buyer's application, inspected the vehicle and submitted a report. The commission relied on the report, along with the buyer's affidavit and documents, including the vehicle invoice and legal notice."It clearly shows that the vehicle's upper portion, left door and bonnet are repainted and due to the painting work it lost its original painting quality," the order recorded.The report also noted differences in colour matching on the repainted portions. The order said the expert had found that the interior roof lining was loose and some parts were lifted.The commission estimated expense for rectifying the roof-lining defects was Rs 50,000, while repainting the upper portion, bonnet and left door would cost more than Rs 1.5 lakh."The painting of vehicle in upper portion bonnet, left door incurred an amount over Rs. 1,50,000/-, so it is clear that the vehicle is used and looked as in a good quality one it occurs Rs. 50,000 + Rs.1,50,000/- as the expenses for curing the defect," the commission concluded.The commission held that the dealer's failure to address the buyer's grievance amounted to deficiency in service and an unfair trade practice. It concluded that the buyer was entitled to relief based on the expert report and the evidence placed on record.Final orderThe commission partly allowed the complaint and directed the dealer to either replace the defective car with a new one or pay the specified repair expenses."The opposite party is further directed to pay Rs.1,50,000/- as compensation for mental agony caused to the complainant and Rs.10,000/- as litigation cost within 30 days of receipt of this order," the commission added.The directions mean the dealer must:Take back the car and replace it with a new one, or pay Rs 2 lakh towards the specified repairs.Pay Rs 1.5 lakh as compensation for mental agony.Pay Rs 10,000 towards litigation costs.The dealer has been directed to comply within 30 days of receiving the order. If it fails to pay the Rs 2 lakh repair amount, that amount will carry interest at 12 percent annually from the date of the order until realisation.

articles.title: 'The Fault in Our Stars' author John Green and his family helped fund a Sierra Leone maternity centre; when it opened in February 2026, 27 patients arrived and 13 babies were born in 24 hours
articles.summary: When a new maternity centre opened in Sierra Leone in February 2026, its first day brought a striking measure of demand for care: 27 patients arrived and
articles.body: When a new maternity centre opened in Sierra Leone in February 2026, its first day brought a striking measure of demand for care: 27 patients arrived and 13 babies were born within 24 hours. The facility, supported by bestselling author John Green, his brother Hank Green and their families and supporters, was built to expand access to specialised maternal and newborn healthcare in a country that continues to face serious challenges in preventing deaths related to pregnancy and childbirth.The Paul E. Farmer Maternal Center of Excellence opened to patients on February 14, 2026, on the campus of Koidu Government Hospital in Kono District. According to Partners In Health (PIH), the nonprofit organisation supporting the project, seven of the 13 babies born during the centre’s first 24 hours were delivered by caesarean section, while six were born vaginally. The opening marked the transition from years of planning and construction to providing inpatient care for women and newborns.How John Green became involvedGreen, best known for writing 'The Fault in Our Stars', became involved in the maternal health initiative after learning about the challenges facing women in Sierra Leone. According to PIH, a 2017 article in The New Yorker helped bring the issue to his attention.In 2018, Green and his wife, Sarah Green, visited Koidu Government Hospital and were inspired by the vision for a specialised maternal healthcare facility. His brother Hank Green and Hank’s wife, Katherine, also joined the effort to advance maternal health through advocacy and fundraising. The Green family and their supporters pledged to raise $25 million to help make the centre a reality, PIH says. The campaign brought together the brothers’ public platforms and a community of supporters around a project intended to address preventable maternal deaths.The facility was named the Paul E. Farmer Maternal Center of Excellence in honour of the late physician and anthropologist Paul Farmer, who co-founded Partners In Health and championed healthcare access for underserved communities. The Greens’ involvement was part of a broader collaboration rather than a project funded or built by the family alone. Sierra Leone’s Ministry of Health, PIH, construction partner Build Health International, local health officials and community leaders all played roles in developing the centre.What happened on opening dayThe centre began receiving its first patients at 10 am on February 14. The early admissions quickly demonstrated why specialised maternity services were needed.One of the first patients was Wulimatu Koroma, a 25-year-old woman who had travelled from Waterloo, about five hours away by road. At 36 weeks pregnant, she was experiencing chest pain and was admitted to the antenatal ward for continued monitoring. Another early arrival, Fatmata Jalloh from Kono District, was 42 weeks pregnant. Doctors found that the protective fluid surrounding her baby had fallen to a dangerously low level, requiring an emergency caesarean section. She later delivered a healthy baby boy.The centre also received a referral involving a 17-year-old patient, Fanta Jimmy, who was suffering from severe pre-eclampsia and whose baby was in distress. Clinicians prioritised her emergency caesarean section. She delivered the first baby born inside the new centre at 1.21 pm. The premature newborn, weighing 1.72 kilograms, was transferred to the neonatal intensive care unit for specialised care. These cases illustrated the importance of having trained staff, operating theatres and newborn intensive care available under one roof.A specialised facility for mothers and newbornsThe centre expanded the services available at Koidu Government Hospital, increasing the capacity of its existing 48-bed maternal ward and special-care baby unit to a 120-bed facility. It includes three operating theatres and Sierra Leone’s first neonatal intensive care unit, according to PIH.The facility is also equipped with a piped medical gas system, including oxygen, outside the capital, Freetown. Such infrastructure can be critical when newborns need respiratory support or women require urgent surgery.Beyond medical equipment, the centre has been designed to make care more accessible and respectful. It includes dedicated spaces where birth companions can support women during childbirth and a dormitory where mothers can remain close to newborns receiving intensive care. Construction began in April 2021 and took four years. Sierra Leone’s President Julius Maada Bio and First Lady Fatima Maada Bio officially inaugurated the facility on October 25, 2025. Staff then underwent further training and preparations before the centre began admitting patients in February 2026.Why the centre matters for Sierra LeoneSierra Leone has faced a substantial burden of maternal mortality. PIH says women in the country face a one-in-74 lifetime risk of dying in childbirth, underscoring the need for improved access to skilled maternity services and emergency obstetric care. Deaths related to pregnancy and childbirth can occur when complications such as severe bleeding, high blood pressure disorders or obstructed labour are not identified and treated quickly. Access to trained midwives, doctors, surgical facilities, blood supplies and newborn intensive care can make a difference when emergencies arise.The new centre is intended not only to treat patients but also to strengthen the wider health system through clinical training and improved standards of care. Its impact will depend on sustained staffing, reliable supplies, referral networks and the ability of women from remote communities to reach the facility when they need it.You use AI every day. articles.title: Britain built a 70-foot water tower disguised as a house in 1923; its 50,000-gallon tank was damaged by a wartime shell before the landmark became a holiday home
articles.summary: In the English village of Thorpeness, a 70-foot structure built to store water was designed to resemble a house perched above the trees.
articles.body: In the English village of Thorpeness, a 70-foot structure built to store water was designed to resemble a house perched above the trees. Completed in 1923, the building concealed a tank with an original capacity of 50,000 gallons, while the structure below provided living accommodation. Known as the House in the Clouds, it was part of the development of Thorpeness, a planned holiday village on the Suffolk coast. Glencairn Stuart Ogilvie, the owner and developer of the Thorpeness Estate, conceived the village and commissioned architects to help realise its distinctive design. Historic England credits Frederick Forbes Glennie with the building’s 1923 design, commissioned as part of Glencairn Stuart Ogilvie’s development of Thorpeness. Its timber weatherboarding, gabled roof and domestic-style windows helped it fit the village’s unusual architectural character. More than a century later, the building remains a landmark, despite no longer serving its original purpose as a water tower.House in the Clouds: how Thorpeness disguised a water towerThe House in the Clouds was built to provide a water supply for Thorpeness. Its unusual appearance reflected the character of the village, which Ogilvie developed as a holiday destination with buildings designed to create a distinctive landscape rather than a conventional resort. The building’s Historic England listing describes a steel-frame structure clad in weatherboarding, topped by a pantiled, gabled roof. The lower part consists of a five-storey tower, while the upper section, supported by arched corner braces, housed the water tank. Windows were incorporated into the structure, including casement windows and projecting bay windows.The original tank held 50,000 gallons. According to the property’s official history, water was pumped from a well using the neighbouring windmill, with a petrol engine available as an alternative when wind conditions were insufficient. The elevated tank formed part of the water-supply system developed for the village. The building was initially called the Gazebo. Mrs Malcolm Mason, a children’s author and friend of Ogilvie, christened it the House in the Clouds. The property’s history records that a poem she wrote in 1923 was inspired by the building. Its new name captured the appearance of a house seemingly suspended above the surrounding trees. Historic England, which designated the building Grade II listed in 1995, describes it as a landmark and the best-known building in the resort village. Its combination of domestic architecture and water-storage infrastructure has helped preserve its distinctive identity.Wartime damage changed the water tower’s capacityThe building was damaged during the Second World War. According to the property’s official history, an English Bofors anti-aircraft shell passed through the tank’s south-eastern corner in 1943 while the gun was firing at a V1 flying bomb. The shell damaged the tank, and two women, the Miss Humphreys, were occupying the accommodation below and were asleep at the time. The subsequent repairs reduced the tank’s capacity from 50,000 gallons to 30,000 gallons. The property’s history records that sections of the tank’s existing steel were used in the repair. The reduction meant that the tower could hold 20,000 fewer gallons than it had originally been designed to store.The building’s water-supply arrangements also evolved over the following decades. An electric pump replaced the petrol engine in 1953, according to the property’s history. By 1963, a wider water supply had been introduced to the area, although the tank continued to be used for storage for a period afterwards. The tower eventually ceased to serve its original function. The property’s history places the end of its use for local water storage in 1977. The tank itself was removed in 1979, opening the way for the former storage space to become part of the house. Refurbishment of the interior and restoration of the garden began in 1987. These changes allowed the structure to survive beyond the purpose for which it had been built. Rather than remaining a working water tower, it became a house whose unusual upper section no longer needed to accommodate a large volume of water.From water infrastructure to holiday accommodationToday, the House in the Clouds operates as holiday accommodation. Its official accommodation page lists five bedrooms distributed across the second, third and fourth floors, with a games room on the fifth floor. The different levels allow guests to experience a building whose layout developed from its original combination of a water tank and living space. The property stands on Uplands Road in Thorpeness, in Suffolk, close to the village’s golf course and Meare, the artificial lake created as part of the resort’s development. Visitors can find practical details through the property’s official location page.The building’s appeal comes from the contrast between its appearance and its original function. From a distance, its roof and weatherboarded exterior resemble a house elevated above the village. Its history, however, is tied to a practical need: storing and supplying water to the developing community. The House in the Clouds is an example of how infrastructure can become part of a place’s architectural identity. Built in 1923, damaged during wartime, altered when its water-storage role ended, and later adapted for holiday use, it has remained a recognisable feature of Thorpeness. Its original purpose has disappeared, but the structure continues to serve a new one while retaining the appearance that made it unusual in the first place.You use AI every day. articles.title: In 2000, Ralph Lauren’s company announced a $5 million gift for a Harlem cancer centre; it opened in 2003 and brought screenings, treatment and practical support to an underserved community
articles.summary: American fashion designer Ralph Lauren's company in 2010 announced a $5 million donation to establish a cancer care centre in Harlem, New York, where many
articles.body: American fashion designer Ralph Lauren's company in 2010 announced a $5 million donation to establish a cancer care centre in Harlem, New York, where many residents faced difficulties accessing medical treatment. The centre opened in 2003 through a partnership involving Polo Ralph Lauren Corporation, Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center (MSK) and North General Hospital. It was set up to provide cancer screenings, diagnosis, treatment and support to people who had limited access to healthcare.According to Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center, the initiative came after Lauren met Dr Harold Freeman, a cancer surgeon who had spent years working with patients from poor and underserved communities. Freeman had seen many women arrive at hospitals with advanced breast cancer, sometimes after struggling for months to obtain medical help. Their experiences showed him that the problem was not always a lack of willingness to seek treatment, but the difficulties patients faced in reaching it.Some women had been unable to get timely medical attention because of insurance problems, transport difficulties or childcare responsibilities. Others did not know where to seek help. Freeman discussed these problems with Lauren during a meeting arranged through Memorial Sloan Kettering.Recalling their conversation years later, Freeman said Lauren stood up, shook his hand and told him, "I will help you." A few days later, Freeman received a call informing him that Lauren wanted to contribute $5 million towards establishing a cancer centre in Harlem.Cancer centre opened in 2003The Ralph Lauren Center for Cancer Care and Prevention opened in 2003, with Freeman serving as its first medical director.At the time, Lauren explained why he had decided to support the project. "I am inspired by Dr. Freeman's commitment to improving the healthcare and lives of the poor and underserved, not only in Harlem but across the nation," he said.Lauren added that Freeman's work had made him more aware of the community's needs and that he hoped the centre could become a model for similar facilities elsewhere in the United States.The centre initially offered cancer education, screening, diagnostic services, treatment and referrals. Its planned services covered breast, prostate, lung, cervical and colon cancers.An important part of the programme was patient navigation, an approach developed by Freeman to help people move through the healthcare system. Patient navigators assist individuals during their treatment and help them deal with practical problems, including transport, language barriers and difficulties arranging appointments.Focused on more than treatmentThe centre was designed to make cancer care more accessible and comfortable for residents who might otherwise struggle to receive treatment.According to MSK, the facility offered a welcoming environment, with signs in English and Spanish and staff members who could communicate in multiple languages. The aim was to help patients feel comfortable seeking medical assistance.Its services eventually included screenings for breast, prostate, cervical, skin and lung cancers, alongside community health fairs, educational programmes and nutrition counselling.The approach built on Freeman's earlier work at the Breast Examination Center of Harlem, which provided free breast and cervical cancer screening to women who were uninsured or had inadequate insurance.By the time Lauren's donation was announced, that programme had served more than 125,000 women over approximately two decades.The new centre sought to extend this work by combining screening and diagnosis with treatment and continued patient support.The Ralph Lauren Center faced a major change in 2010 when North General Hospital closed. Memorial Sloan Kettering subsequently became its sole institutional partner, while Lauren continued supporting the facility through the Ralph Lauren Corporate Foundation.In 2019, the centre officially became an ambulatory care centre of MSK, strengthening its connection with the cancer institution.Its partnership with MSK's Immigrant Health and Cancer Disparities Service has helped extend cancer-related services beyond the centr. A Mobile Health Unit provides screenings, education and counselling in New York City neighbourhoods where access to healthcare and transport is limited.Further $25 million commitment Nearly two decades after the centre opened, the Ralph Lauren Corporate Foundation announced another major commitment.In 2022, the foundation pledged $25 million to support the existing Harlem centre and establish four additional centres across the United States.You use AI every day. articles.title: ‘Ja nahi rahe the, andar ghus gaye’: Ashutosh Ranka on CJP members’ Jantar Mantar detention
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) leader Ashutosh Ranka on Tuesday alleged that party members had entered Jantar Mantar before being detained by
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) leader Ashutosh Ranka on Tuesday alleged that party members had entered Jantar Mantar before being detained by Delhi Police, responding to a user on X who said they had been detained while going to the protest site.“सर जा नहीं रहे थे, अंदर घुस गए,” Ranka wrote, roughly translating to, “Sir, they weren’t just going there; they entered inside.”The remark came after CJP leaders Saurav Das and Ranka were detained by Delhi Police while attempting to reach Jantar Mantar, police sources said.CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke also claimed that several other members, including Ajinkya Shinde, had been detained.CJP members jump gate to enter Jantar MantarIn a post on X, Dipke said CJP members carrying the national flag had entered Jantar Mantar before police detained them.“Cockroaches with the Tiranga sneaked into Jantar Mantar early this morning before they were picked up by Delhi Police,” Dipke said.He named Ranka, Das, Shinde and other team members as among those detained.“You cannot denotify the resistance,” Dipke added, tagging Prime Minister Narendra Modi.Dipke also shared a video purportedly showing CJP members jumping over a gate to enter Jantar Mantar and raising slogans such as “Bharat Mata ki Jai”. Police personnel are seen rushing towards them and taking them away.Security tightened in DelhiThe detentions came amid heightened security in the national capital following calls for demonstrations against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.Delhi Police has deployed a large number of personnel across the city to maintain law and order. articles.title: Watch: Team CJP climb barricades to 'reclaim' Jantar Mantar after protest ban
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) leaders Ashutosh Ranka, Saurav Das and Ajinkya Shinde, along with other party volunteers, sneaked inside the Jantar
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) leaders Ashutosh Ranka, Saurav Das and Ajinkya Shinde, along with other party volunteers, sneaked inside the Jantar Mantar protest site in New Delhi on Tuesday morning and were detained by Delhi Police.CJP leader Saurav Das posted a video on social media showing him and other protesters raising slogans inside the Jantar Mantar campus. He claimed that they had “reclaimed Jantar Mantar”.In a video shared by CJP leader Ashutosh Ranka, protesters were seen climbing over barricades and entering the Jantar Mantar campus.In a post on X, CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke said several party members including Ajinkya Shinde, had been detained by Delhi Police."Cockroaches with the Tiranga sneaked into Jantar Mantar early this morning before they were picked up by Delhi Police," Dipke said."You cannot denotify the resistance," he added, tagging Prime Minister Narendra Modi.This comes a day after Delhi Police removed Jantar Mantar from the list of designated protest venues, ending its long-standing status as a site for demonstrations in the national capital.In a notice issued by Delhi Police Commissioner Anurag Kumar, the police said the Ministry of Home Affairs had constituted a committee to identify suitable alternative venues where citizens could exercise their right to organise protests and demonstrations. The decision was taken based on the committee’s recommendations.The three designated venues are Ramlila Ground in Central Delhi, Burari Ground in North Delhi and CBD Ground in East Delhi. Delhi Police said a detailed and revised standard operating procedure (SOP) governing protests at these locations would be issued separately.The order partially modifies Standing Order No. L&O/48/22, dated April 28, 2022."Detailed and revised SOP for organizing protest/demonstrations at these three venues will be issued separately. This is in partial modification of earlier Standing Order No. L&O/48/22 dated 28.04.2022," the notice read.The move comes amid protests in the national capital demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Hurricane Simon pounds Mexico's Pacific coast; Rachel's remnants flood US Southwest
articles.summary: Hurricane Simon battered Mexico’s Pacific coast on Monday with heavy rain and strong winds, while the remnants of Tropical Storm Rachel left communities
articles.body: Hurricane Simon battered Mexico’s Pacific coast on Monday with heavy rain and strong winds, while the remnants of Tropical Storm Rachel left communities flooded in the US Southwest. The weather systems caused deaths, damaged homes and roads, and forced evacuations across affected areas.Simon, a Category 2 hurricane, remained offshore as its outer bands lashed communities near Puerto Vallarta. In Guerrero state, the storm uprooted trees and electricity poles, blocked roads and flooded homes, including in the port city of Acapulco, governor Evelyn Salgado said.Reports claim that five people have died due to the hurricane.The US national hurricane center said Simon was expected to remain a hurricane through midweek before making landfall near Sinaloa on Thursday. Rainfall of 5 to 10 inches (12.7 to 25.4 cm) over west-central Mexico in the coming days could trigger life-threatening floods and mudslides.In Puerto Vallarta, workers removed wooden panels from storefronts and businesses reopened as rainfall eased. However, the international airport suspended operations until Tuesday morning.“Personally, I think we should remain on alert because we don’t really know whether it will arrive, move elsewhere or dissipate,” Noelia Carrillo told news agency AP.Rachel triggers deadly flooding in Baja CaliforniaIn Baja California, rescuers searched parts of Ensenada on Monday after floodwaters swept away vehicles and damaged homes. Residents described being caught off guard by the sudden surge of water after heavy rain knocked out electricity.Landslides and overflowing rivers also cut off several communities across the state.The Mexican military used helicopters to rescue 32 people, including 22 foreigners and 13 children, from a ranch in Ensenada. State secretary of security general Laureano Carrillo said some of those rescued were missionaries attending a meeting at the ranch, including Germans and Americans.At least 10 people were reported missing and a young girl was killed in the aftermath of Rachel, Baja California governor Marina del Pilar Ávila said. Around 14,000 federal and state personnel had been deployed to assist residents and respond to the emergency.Rachel weakened into a post-tropical cyclone as it moved north into Southern California. It brought unusually large waves that damaged a boardwalk and battered homes in Long Beach, forcing some residents to evacuate.Las Vegas records October rainfall highThe storm’s remnants also caused flooding in Las Vegas, which recorded 1.08 inches (2.74 cm) of rain by Sunday morning, tying its all-time daily rainfall record for October. The previous record was set in 1947, according to the US national weather service.Videos shared on social media showed floodwaters rushing through a street near the Las Vegas Strip, with casinos and a Ferris wheel visible in the background.Flood advisories were largely lifted by late Monday across Utah, Arizona and other parts of the Southwest.Meanwhile, power restoration continued in the US Southeast after Hurricane Isaias struck the region. At least four deaths have been linked to the storm, which made landfall as a Category 2 hurricane near Destin, Florida, on Friday before moving into Alabama with tropical-force winds.Drier conditions were forecast across parts of the mid-Atlantic and Southeast over the next few days, although temperatures were expected to remain above normal in some areas.You use AI every day. articles.title: Kargil War widow and BJP veteran Sudha Yadav is new Karnataka governor
articles.summary: BENGALURU: With incumbent Thaawar Chand Gehlot completing five years in office, President Droupadi Murmu on Monday appointed Kargil War widow and BJP
articles.body: BENGALURU: With incumbent Thaawar Chand Gehlot completing five years in office, President Droupadi Murmu on Monday appointed Kargil War widow and BJP leader Sudha Yadav, 61, next governor of Karnataka.Yadav, a former MP and member of BJP's Parliamentary Board, will be the state's second woman governor after VS Ramadevi, who held office from Dec 1999 to Aug 2002.Yadav holds a doctorate in chemistry from Roorkee University, now IIT-Roorkee. She entered politics after her husband, BSF deputy commandant Sukhbir Singh Yadav, was killed during the 1999 Kargil War.BJP fielded her from Mahendragarh in Haryana in 1999 Lok Sabha elections, which she won. She represented the constituency until 2004.She subsequently served as BJP national secretary and headed its OBC Morcha.She was a member of National Commission for Backward Classes from 2019 to 2022.In Aug 2022, she was inducted into the BJP's Parliamentary Board, its highest decision-making body.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Bengaluru | Silver Rate in Bengaluru | Bank Holidays in Bengaluru | Public Holidays in Bengaluru | Bengaluru AQI | Weather in Bengaluru | Petrol Price in Bengaluru | Diesel Price in Bengaluru | CNG Price in Bengaluru | LPG Price in BengaluruStay updated with the latest Bengaluru news. articles.title: 5 killed, several injured as passenger train derails in Pakistan's Punjab
articles.summary: At least five people were killed and several others injured after a passenger train derailed in Pakistan's Punjab province early Tuesday, Pakistan-based
articles.body: At least five people were killed and several others injured after a passenger train derailed in Pakistan's Punjab province early Tuesday, Pakistan-based Geo News reported.The Rehman Baba Express, travelling from the southern port city of Karachi to the northwestern city of Peshawar, derailed in Sher Shah, Punjab province, news agency AP reported, citing Pakistan Railways spokesperson Kaleem Akhtar.The injured were taken to Nishtar Hospital in Multan for treatment, while rescue teams continued operations at the accident site.The accident took place at around 5.15am, according to Geo News.Pakistan President Asif Ali Zardari and Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif expressed grief over the deaths in separate statements and directed authorities to ensure the best possible medical care for the injured.Train accidents are relatively common in Pakistan, where the railway system has suffered from decades of underinvestment, outdated tracks and ageing signalling systems.In 2023, 10 carriages of a passenger train derailed in southern Pakistan, killing 30 people and injuring more than 90 others.You use AI every day. articles.summary: CHHATRAPATI SAMBHAJINAGAR: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke on Tuesday said protests would continue across the country until Chief
articles.body: CHHATRAPATI SAMBHAJINAGAR: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke on Tuesday said protests would continue across the country until Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar resigned, alleging that Prime Minister Narendra Modi was afraid of public protests.Reacting to the de-notification of Jantar Mantar as a designated protest site, Dipke said the move would not stop demonstrations, but lead to similar protest sites emerging across the country."Narendra Modi's fear is evident from the fact that he has removed Jantar Mantar as a designated protest site. He thinks protests will stop if Jantar Mantar is no longer a designated protest site, but that is not going to happen. Jantar Mantars will now emerge across the country," Dipke said."Narendra Modi's problem is not with Jantar Mantar as a location, but with protests. We must understand this," he added.Meanwhile, Delhi Police detained Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) leaders Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka on Tuesday as they attempted to reach Jantar Mantar, police said.In a post on X, CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke claimed that several other team members, including Ajinkya Shinde, had also been detained."Cockroaches with the Tiranga sneaked into Jantar Mantar early this morning before they were picked up by Delhi Police," Dipke said.“You cannot denotify the resistance, Narendra Modi,” Dipke said in the post.Stay updated with the latest Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar news. articles.title: Madras HC upholds TN assembly speaker's decision to accept resignations of 6 AIADMK MLAs
articles.summary: CHENNAI: In a reprieve to the ruling TVK govt in Tamil Nadu, the Madras High Court on Friday dismissed a petition filed by AIADMK whip Agri S
articles.body: CHENNAI: In a reprieve to the ruling TVK govt in Tamil Nadu, the Madras High Court on Friday dismissed a petition filed by AIADMK whip Agri S Krishnamurthy and others challenging the Assembly speaker’s decision to accept the resignations of six AIADMK MLAs.The six MLAs cross-voted in favour of the TVK govt during a confidence motion and later joined the ruling TVK.The first bench of Chief Justice Sushrut Arvind Dharmadhikari and Justice G Arul Murugan held that the resignation tendered by the defecting MLAs was genuine and voluntary and in terms of provision enshrined under the Tenth Schedule of the Constitution."The speaker of Tamil Nadu legislative Assembly was not required to undertake a roving or fishing inquiry to the alleged motives behind them. Apparently, their acceptance and the consequential declaration of vacancies are constitutionally valid," the court said.The pendency of disqualification proceedings did not constitutionally bar the speaker from accepting the resignations, as resignation and disqualification are two distinct constitutional processes. The speaker was therefore competent to accept the resignation notwithstanding the pending disqualification proceedings, the judges added."The acceptance of resignations does not render the pending disqualification proceedings academic or infructuous. The speaker shall still finally adjudicate and decide the disqualification proceedings, and such determination shall carry the consequences prescribed under the Tenth Schedule of the Constitution," the bench said.The court asserted that the HC possesses the power under Article 226 of the Constitution to intervene where the speaker fails to decide disqualification proceedings within a reasonable period."In the peculiar circumstances, a time-bound mandamus is being issued directing the speaker to conclude the disqualification proceedings finally within two months," the court said.The primary contention of the petitioners was that the speaker should not have accepted the resignations of the MLAs before deciding the disqualification proceedings for crossvoting in favour of the TVK govt violating party whip.According to the petitioners, conducting an inquiry to ascertain whether the resignations were made voluntarily or not was not merely a procedural formality but a constitutional obligation, and that no meaningful inquiry had actually been conducted.Opposing the pleas, the speaker contended that acceptance of the resignations would not automatically render the pending disqualification proceedings ineffective. If an MLA wishes to resign, he or she cannot be compelled to continue in office. Refusal to accept such resignations would amount to a failure on the part of the speaker to discharge a constitutional duty, he said.The speaker also argued that he is constitutionally duty bound to accept the resignation tendered by an MLA if it is done voluntarily. No one can compel a legislator to continue in his/her post, he said.The MLAs contended that defection proceedings would arise only if an MLA continued to enjoy the privileges of office while extending support to another political party. articles.title: JNU row: BJP women MPs to meet President Murmu over sexual harassment charges against Congress MP
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: A delegation of BJP women MPs will meet President Droupadi Murmu on Tuesday over sexual harassment allegations against Congress MP Angomcha
articles.body: NEW DELHI: A delegation of BJP women MPs will meet President Droupadi Murmu on Tuesday over sexual harassment allegations against Congress MP Angomcha Bimol Akoijam, news agency ANI reported citing sources.The development comes a day after BJP Mahila Morcha workers staged protests across the country, demanding action against Akoijam, who represents Inner Manipur in the Lok Sabha.Protesters also burnt effigies of leader of opposition in Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi and accused the Congress leadership of remaining silent on the matter.The protests followed reports that Jawaharlal Nehru University (JNU) had dismissed Akoijam from his position as a professor after an internal committee examined allegations by 11 female students.The BJP has claimed that the committee found the allegations to be true. The claims have not been independently verified in the material available.Delhi Police registered an FIR following a complaint by JNU's chief security officer. The case was registered at Vasant Kunj North police station under Sections 75, 75(1)(i), 75(1)(iv) and 79 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS). Police said the investigation was underway.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Peaceful protest fundamental to democracy, will review police action against protesters: Kharge
articles.summary: BENGALURU: Karnataka home minister Priyank Kharge Tuesday said he’ll review Bengaluru police’s handling of anti-SIR protesters who were detained on
articles.body: BENGALURU: Karnataka home minister Priyank Kharge Tuesday said he’ll review Bengaluru police’s handling of anti-SIR protesters who were detained on Monday, when police forcibly removed demonstrators and manhandled journalists covering the action.“The right to peaceful protest is fundamental to our democracy. It must be respected, protected and never suppressed,” Kharge said in a post on X. “I have issued instructions to the police to ensure that no peaceful demonstration is disrupted,” he added.Late on Monday, chief minister DK Shivakumar, had posted on X asking Bengaluru police commissioner to “look into this and ensure that the right to peaceful protest is protected”.Kharge also appealed to protesters to cooperate with the police and inform authorities in advance to ensure their safety and protect the rights of others. “The police are here to protect your rights, not to stand in the way of your voice,” he said.The announcement comes after dozens of protesters, including students, lawyers, activists, academics and senior citizens, were detained near KR Circle as they sought to march to the chief electoral officer’s office. They were demanding that the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls be scrapped and Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar resign.The action also saw photojournalists covering the protest being assaulted and other journalists manhandled. Plainclothes personnel were among those seen acting aggressively towards protesters and journalists.An activist group, My Vote, My Right, said police confiscated placards and began detaining protesters before they could start the march. Its press release said people were pushed, dragged and forcibly taken away in buses. Police personnel were also seen beating young protesters and pulling at the clothes of women protesters, the group said.One photojournalist was beaten by four police personnel, while three other journalists were manhandled, according to the group.A photojournalist who witnessed the police action said an officer asked him to delete footage he had recorded of police assaulting students inside a bus. As journalists continued filming the detention of women protesters, police personnel objected.“One person came and said, delete it,” the photojournalist recounted. He said police personnel subsequently grabbed his phone, pushed him to the ground and threw the phone aside. Another officer pulled him by the collar, while personnel pushed him from behind and hit him on the leg. An officer also threatened to put him in jail.The incident had drawn criticism on social media, including from Arpita Das, associate professor of writing at Ashoka University, who said her daughter and a friend had been detained after joining the protest. She questioned why this was happening in a Congress-ruled state when young people were supporting the party’s position on SIR. Shivakumar’s X post was in response to Das’ post.The detentions in Bengaluru, incidentally happened on a day both Shivakumar and Kharge were protesting against SIR and police action against demonstrators in Delhi.On Monday, DCP (Central) Akshay M Hakay had said protesters had assembled near KR Circle without permission or prior intimation, contrary to high court directions that demonstrations be held at designated places. Police initially asked them to move to Freedom Park, but they did not comply and were taken into preventive custody before being released, he said.Hakay said police had acted with restraint and sensitivity. Acknowledging friction between police personnel and journalists, he described it as “completely unintentional” and said it had occurred in “straining circumstances”.Kharge Tuesday said: “Our responsibility is not merely to maintain law and order, but to create an environment where every citizen can express dissent freely, peacefully and without fear… In a democracy, peaceful dissent is not a threat to law and order. It is a right that law and order must protect,” he said.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: SC stays criminal defamation trial against Rahul Gandhi in ‘Chowkidar chor hai’ case
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Tuesday stayed trial court proceedings against Lok Sabha leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi in a criminal defamation case
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Tuesday stayed trial court proceedings against Lok Sabha leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi in a criminal defamation case over his alleged ‘Chowkidar chor hai’ remarks against Prime Minister Narendra Modi.The court also issued a notice on Rahul's plea challenging the Bombay high court’s order refusing to quash the defamation case."Issue notice returnable in four weeks. Further proceedings before the trial court shall remain stayed," news agency PTI quoted the bench saying.Senior advocate Abhishek Singhvi, appearing for Rahul, cited earlier Supreme Court judgments and argued that the law on the matter was settled. The bench posted the case for further hearing after four weeks.The Bombay HC, on September 8, refused to quash the summons issued to Rahul in 2019, dismissing his challenge to a Girgaum magistrate’s order dated August 28, 2019.However, it extended its 2021 order directing the magistrate to defer proceedings for six weeks to allow the Congress leader to approach the Supreme Court.The complaint was filed by BJP worker Mahesh Shrishrimal over Rahul's speech in Rajasthan on September 20, 2018. Shrishrimal argued that, as a BJP member, he was aggrieved by remarks against the party’s leader.The complaint alleged that Rahul's statements defamed PM Modi and amounted to allegations against BJP members and Indian citizens associated with him.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: In 2019, a Michael Dell-backed firm bought the Boca Raton resort for $875 million and later spent about $375 million upgrading it; now 40% of its first 75 luxury condos have been claimed
articles.summary: A $875 million investment in a historic Florida resort is expanding into the luxury residential market, with wealthy buyers showing early interest in its
articles.body: A $875 million investment in a historic Florida resort is expanding into the luxury residential market, with wealthy buyers showing early interest in its planned condominiums. According to the New York Post, around 40% of the first 75 luxury residences planned at The Boca Raton resort have already been claimed. The project follows the 2019 acquisition of the property by a firm backed by billionaire Michael Dell and approximately $375 million in subsequent renovations and upgrades, as reported by Bloomberg in April 2026.The development marks a new chapter for The Boca Raton, a landmark property that has traditionally operated as a luxury resort and private members' club. By introducing privately owned residences within the resort, its owners are seeking to combine high-end real estate with the services and amenities associated with an established hospitality destination.From a historic inn to a luxury residential addressBoca Raton, a coastal city in Palm Beach County, Florida, has long been associated with affluent residents, retirees and resort living. The Boca Raton's history dates back to February 6, 1926, when the original Cloister Inn opened its doors. Designed by architect Addison Mizner, the 100-room hotel helped establish the Mediterranean Revival architectural style that became associated with South Florida's luxury properties.Over the decades, the original inn evolved into a sprawling resort offering accommodation, leisure facilities and membership-based amenities. The property is marking its centenary in 2026, making the planned residential development part of a broader transformation at a landmark destination.The new residences will introduce a different ownership model, allowing buyers to purchase homes within the resort grounds rather than relying solely on hotel stays or club membership. The reported sales suggest that the concept has attracted early interest among affluent buyers.Prices begin at $8.95 millionThe residences are positioned at the upper end of the luxury housing market. According to the New York Post, prices range from $8.95 million to more than $20 million, with the starting price considerably higher than the approximately $4 million figure discussed when the project was initially proposed.The planned collection includes penthouses, terrace residences and villas with private gardens and swimming pools. The homes target buyers seeking private residential space alongside access to resort-style services. Reported amenities include butler service, a rooftop swimming pool, a spa, a gym and a members-only lounge. Buyers will also be offered a Residential Club Membership that extends to their families, adding a membership component to the appeal of owning a home within the property.A $375 million renovation programmeThe residential project follows a substantial investment in the resort. According to Bloomberg, the Michael Dell-backed investment firm had spent approximately $375 million on renovations and upgrades since acquiring the property for $875 million in 2019.The investment group is associated with BDT & MSD Partners, formed through the combination of MSD Partners, linked to Dell, and BDT & Co., founded by banker Byron Trott. Dell is the founder and chief executive of Dell Technologies. The condominium project adds another potential revenue stream to the resort's existing operations, which include accommodation, leisure facilities and private club services.However, the reported 40% figure is an early sales indicator, not evidence that the project has already generated a profit. The residences remain under development, and their financial performance will depend on factors including final sales, construction costs and demand as the project progresses.Moreover, the firm had secured a $1 billion refinancing for the resort. That financing is separate from condominium sales and does not, by itself, establish the profitability of the residential development.The development is being designed by Hart Howerton, with interiors by Pembrooke & Ives. The planned eight-storey building is expected to enter construction in 2026, with completion targeted for 2029.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.
